predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a NATO Article 5 invocation signals a material escalation of armed conflict involving a NATO member (likely Russia/eastern-flank incident). Defense procurement expectations rise immediately on escalation, and defense equities are the most direct, high-beta beneficiary. European-domiciled names (Rheinmetall, BAE, Leonardo, Thales) captured by EUAD are the most exposed to an eastern-flank crisis. A genuine escalation can move these names several percent in a session, though reaching 700bps in 12h requires a confirmed hard-news catalyst, not just a probability drift.

predictions.reasoning: An escalation sharp enough to raise Article 5 odds would trigger a risk-off move in the most directly exposed regional equity bloc. European large caps (banks, industrials, autos) would sell off on war-escalation fears, energy-supply risk and EUR weakness. FEZ is a liquid proxy for the eurozone equity complex. The move is opposite-signed to defense: the broad index falls while defense names rise. A 700bps broad-index drop in 12h would require a severe, clearly public shock; more plausibly a few hundred bps.

evidence_used: Market resolves Yes only if a NATO member formally invokes Article 5 between Nov 5 2025 and Dec 31 2026 — a rare, high-impact collective-defense trigger
Topic is military_conflict, region Europe, implying an eastern-flank/Russia escalation scenario
Historical pattern: escalation news lifts defense equities and pressures broad European risk assets simultaneously
Long resolution horizon means a sharp short-term probability spike would most likely be driven by a discrete escalation event
uncertainty_notes: A 12h window and 700bps threshold are demanding; prediction-market probability drift without hard news rarely moves liquid assets that much
Mapping depends on the probability move being a genuine escalation signal, not thin-liquidity noise on a low-base-rate market
If an escalation is already public, the asset move will have occurred before any prediction-market leak, nullifying the edge

llm_justification.summary: The market measures the probability of a NATO Article 5 invocation, effectively a gauge of European armed-conflict escalation risk. A sharp upward move in that probability maps to higher European defense-equity prices (EUAD) and a risk-off selloff in broad eurozone equities (FEZ), with gold/Bunds bid and EUR softer. Both mappings are directionally confident but the 700bps/12h magnitude bar is high and likely only met with a confirmed hard-news catalyst, so confidence is moderate.
key_assumptions: A sharp probability rise reflects a real escalation event rather than market noise or a single large bettor
Escalation would be Europe/Russia-centric, maximizing exposure of European proxies
Defense equities rise and broad European index falls on the same catalyst (negative correlation holds)
failure_modes: The probability move is driven by low-liquidity speculation with no underlying event, so assets do not move
The escalation is already fully public, meaning asset prices already repriced before any prediction-market leak
Proxy exposure is weaker than assumed — defense ETFs can lag on 'buy the rumor, sell the news' dynamics
A de-escalation or diplomatic resolution reverses the move within the 12h window
Base rate of Article 5 is extremely low; most probability spikes historically revert without asset impact
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
